mappings.raw: k-nearest-neighbors search over possession subsequences with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) as distance function, accelerated by clustering subsequences by start/end pitch cells (7x4 grid of 15m x 17m cells -> 784 origin-destination clusters); expected reward labels come from an XGBoost expected-goals model (500 estimators, learning rate 0.01, max depth 5)

Pre-game pressure: Gradient Boosted Ranking Trees (max_depth: 6, n_estimators: 50) trained on pairwise expert rankings. In-game pressure / win probability: Bayesian temporal stochastic model with logit(theta_t,home) = alpha_t * x_t,home + beta + Ha and logit(theta_t,away) = alpha_t * x_t,away + beta, priors alpha_t ~ N(alpha_{t-1}, sigma^2), beta ~ N(0,10), Ha ~ N(0,10); inference via PyMC3 Auto-Differentiation Variational Inference (ADVI). Contribution rating V(s): inherited from Decroos et al. VAEP framework (22 action types). Action-success classifier (per action type): Gradient Boosted Trees. Next-action contribution predictor (used for ECR|s_i): Gradient Boosted Trees, two heads estimating P(g_{i+1}+ | s_i) and P(g_{i+1}- | s_i) combined as ECR|s_i = [P(g_{i+1}+ | s_i) - P(g_+ | s_{i-1})] - [P(g_{i+1}- | s_i) - P(g_- | s_{i-1})].

Distance-weighted k-nearest-neighbors over historical passes using a learned six-component domain-specific distance function; passes pre-clustered by origin-destination pitch zones; possession-sequence labels produced by an XGBoost expected-goals model trained on shot location, distance to goal center, and angle to goal posts; weights for the distance function learned via Bayesian Optimization (UCB acquisition, 250 iterations, 10 initial weight sets).
L2-regularized linear Support Vector Machine (LIBLINEAR) with asymmetric (class-specific) cost parameters; per-pass value PSV(i,j) = w_i^o + w_j^d + w_ij^od derived from learned model weights.

k-nearest-neighbors over phases using multivariate dynamic time warping (DTW) on (x,y) action sequences; phase rating distributed across actions using an exponential-decay weighting scheme with parameter lambda
Gradient-boosted decision trees (CatBoost), chosen over Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost based on Brier score and ROC AUC comparison

Deep convolutional neural network: three convolutional layers with 32 kernels of size 6x6 and ReLU activations, followed by a fully connected layer of 256 nodes with ReLU, and a single output node V; trained with TD(lambda) (lambda-return) batch reinforcement learning

Graph recurrent neural network (GRNN) over a fully connected graph of all 22 players and the ball; two graph layers (GL) with GRU width 1024; attention functions alpha^type, alpha^v and function f_v have a single hidden layer of 512 units; input feature function phi_I has layers of sizes 128 and 256; Mixture Density Network (MDN) head with K=6 Gaussian components (means mu_k and variances sigma_k via two-layer MLPs of 512 units, ReLU and linear/exponential outputs respectively); value head phi_V is a two-layer MLP with 512 units and linear output. Implemented in TensorFlow.

Decoupled / decomposed model with independently estimated component sub-models: pass and turnover probabilities estimated with logistic regression; action likelihood modeled by a convolutional neural network on top of pitch control and pitch influence surfaces; pass and ball-drive value expectations learned by carefully designed deep neural networks; shot/expected-goals component described as a variant of expected-goals models. All components calibrated for accuracy at the component level as well as at the joint EPV level.

Two-tower stacked LSTM (one tower per home/away team); each tower is a two-layer LSTM with 256 hidden nodes plus an embedding layer and two hidden layers with 256 nodes; outputs normalized via softmax to produce Q_Home, Q_Away, Q_Neither; trained with on-policy Temporal Difference (Sarsa) and a dynamic-possession LSTM trace length (max 10 steps); Adam optimizer with initial learning rate 10E-04 (general) and 10E-05 (fine-tuning). Interpretability via CART mimic regression tree.

XGBoost binary probabilistic classifier (best hyperparameters: 2000 estimators, learning rate 0.01, max depth 4; random state 10; stratified shuffle split 70/30; 10-fold cross-validation). Auxiliary rule-based / geometric components: k-means (k=3) for dynamic formation lines; dynamic Voronoi diagram over defenders' expected positions for defensive area assignment; deterministic attribution rule that distributes the final possession EPV across on-ball actions proportionally to their (positive) value added (effective value added).

Multi Layer Perceptron (MLP) built with Keras; 3 dense hidden layers with 10 neurons each, ELU activation, MAE loss, Adadelta optimizer, trained for 50 epochs; inputs MinMax-scaled with Scikit-Learn's MinMaxScaler

Recurrent neural network with single 64-dim GRU middle layer (ReLU), input 106 x 64 (state 92-dim + action 14-dim), output 64 x 14 Q-values; trained with SARSA TD loss + cross-entropy action-supervision loss (L_AS) + L1 regularization; Adam optimizer; lambda_1 = 0.01, lambda_2 = 0.1

Three-phase pipeline: (1) Learning phase - Linear Support Vector Classifier (LSVC, L2-SVM via scikit-learn svm.LinearSVC) trained on team-aggregated feature vectors to predict match outcome, yielding feature weights w; k-means clustering (k=8) over players' centers of performance (average event positions) with soft-clustering (k-silhouette, delta_s=0.1) for hybrid roles. (2) Rating phase - per-player-match rating computed as scalar product r(u,m) = (1/R) * sum_i w_i * x_i; goal-adjusted rating r*(u,m) = alpha * norm_goals + (1-alpha) * r(u,m); series aggregation via Exponential Weighted Moving Average (EWMA). (3) Ranking phase - role-based rankings R_1,...,R_z assigning a player to role R_i if assigned to it in at least x=40% of matches.

Logistic regression classifier (chosen over non-linear black-box models for interpretability); features hand-crafted from tracking data; tactical and formation context added via tree-structured feature augmentation including k-means clustering on player XY positions

Encoder-decoder convolutional policy network over 11 x 105 x 68 pitch channels with two output heads (softmax selection surface, sigmoid success surface) and a reconstruction decoder; off-policy policy-gradient fine-tuning

CNN-LSTM network (convolutional layers + max pooling + LSTM with 100 memory units + fully connected + softmax) trained with Policy Gradient (PG). A separate CNN-LSTM binary classifier estimates P(score within next 10 actions) used as the reward signal.

Closed-form discrete-time Markov chain over 39 states (2 absorbing states + 7 set pieces + 30 states defined by zonal location and defensive state); transition matrix repeatedly multiplied until absorption probabilities converge

Closed-form Markov-style recurrence xT_{x,y} = (s_{x,y} * g_{x,y}) + (m_{x,y} * sum_{z,w} T_{(x,y)->(z,w)} * xT_{z,w}), solved by fixed-point iteration starting from xT = 0 for all zones; 4-5 iterations sufficient for convergence.

Probabilistic physics-based model decomposed into three conditional components: (1) Potential Pitch Control Field (PPCF) modeling per-player control probability via a differential equation using time-to-intercept (logistic CDF) and ball time-of-flight with aerodynamic drag; (2) Transition model as a 2D normal distribution over next on-ball location scaled by PPCF^alpha; (3) Score model as a monotonic function of distance to goal raised to a power beta. Parameters fit via Bayesian MAP with normally distributed priors.

xT: closed-form Markov chain solved iteratively over an M x N grid (16 x 12 in this paper, converged after 6 iterations). VAEP: two separate XGBoost gradient boosted tree classifiers (one for P_score, one for P_concede) trained on a feature representation of the last three actions plus game context.

Closed-form Markov Decision Process learned per team from event data; Gradient Boosted Trees Ensembles used to predict intended end locations of move actions (to estimate transition probabilities); PRISM probabilistic model checker used to compute properties (e.g., probability of generating a better shot later) and STORM mentioned as an alternative; counterfactual policy alteration via proportional re-weighting of action probabilities; expected number of state visits computed from the MDP fundamental matrix N = (I - Q)^-1.

Hierarchical Bayesian model (Bernoulli/Categorical with Normal log-odds and Half-Normal variances, weakly-informative priors via Gaussian-smoothed counts) fit with PyMC3 ADVI; XGBoost gradient boosted trees ensembles for predicting intended end locations of failed passes and crosses; domain-knowledge post-processing; Bellman value iteration / fundamental matrix for derived quantities; PRISM probabilistic model checking for policy queries.

Two LightGBM gradient-boosted tree models (one per velocity component, x and y), trained over a 61-dimensional covariate vector built from tracking data. Per-instance score p is a closed-form projection (Eq. 1) of the observed velocity onto the predicted velocity direction; season-long P-score is the mean of p across instances scaled by 100% (Eq. 2).
